content.value_statement: Production incidents need fast triage without skipping evidence. This skill guides structured DevOps debugging across logs, metrics, traces, Kubernetes, cloud platforms, and CI/CD systems.
actual_capabilities: Guides incident triage using impact, scope, logs, metrics, traces, and system state.
Supports Kubernetes debugging for pods, services, ingress, storage, and resource constraints.
Helps analyze performance issues across applications, databases, caches, and infrastructure.
Provides cloud troubleshooting coverage for AWS, Azure, GCP, and serverless services.
Frames post-incident work through documentation, monitoring, runbooks, and blameless postmortems.
limitations: It provides guidance and checklists, not automatic access to production systems.
It depends on accurate logs, metrics, traces, and operational context from the user.
It cannot validate vendor-specific account state without tool access or user-provided output.
It should not replace established incident command, change control, or security approval processes.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Outage
use_cases.description: Structure the first response, identify affected services, gather evidence, and select low-risk mitigation steps.

use_cases.title: Debug Kubernetes Failures
use_cases.description: Investigate pod restarts, OOMKills, networking issues, ingress failures, storage problems, and rollout errors.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Turn an incident timeline into root cause findings, monitoring gaps, runbook updates, and long-term reliability actions.

prompt_templates.title: Start Incident Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me triage a production incident. Impact: [users or services affected]. Symptoms: [errors or alerts]. Recent changes: [deploys or config changes]. Available evidence: [logs, metrics, traces, dashboards].

prompt_templates.title: Debug Kubernetes Pods
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot this Kubernetes issue. Namespace: [namespace]. Workload: [deployment or pod]. Symptoms: [restarts, pending pods, errors]. Relevant kubectl output: [events, describe, logs, resource metrics].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Performance Bottlenecks
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this performance problem. Service: [service]. Slow path: [endpoint or job]. Metrics: [latency, CPU, memory, database, queue]. Traces or logs: [key observations]. Build a hypothesis tree and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Postmortem Action Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a postmortem action plan from this incident timeline: [timeline]. Root cause evidence: [facts]. Mitigations applied: [actions]. Monitoring gaps: [gaps]. Separate immediate, preventive, and strategic work.

output_examples.input: A service has 504 errors after a deployment.
output_examples.output: The response would separate impact, recent change validation, load balancer checks, upstream health, rollback criteria, and evidence needed from logs and traces.

output_examples.input: Kubernetes pods are restarting with OOMKilled events.
output_examples.output: The response would compare memory requests, limits, usage trends, application allocation patterns, recent traffic, and safe mitigation options.
The response would produce a timeline review, likely contributing factors, monitoring gaps, runbook updates, owners, and prevention tasks.

best_practices: Provide exact symptoms, timestamps, recent changes, and affected services before asking for root cause analysis.
Share sanitized logs, metrics, traces, events, and command output so recommendations stay evidence based.
Use the skill to plan safe tests and mitigations before applying changes in production.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, tokens, private keys, or unrestricted customer data into prompts.
Do not execute broad or destructive remediation steps without approval and rollback planning.
Do not treat a single log line as root cause without checking related metrics, traces, and recent changes.

faq.question: Can this skill run kubectl or cloud commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides troubleshooting guidance and can interpret output that you provide.

faq.question: Which systems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers observability tools, Kubernetes, cloud platforms, CI/CD, databases, networks, security debugging, and incident response.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, when used with your incident process, access controls, approval rules, and rollback procedures.

faq.question: Does it replace an SRE runbook?
faq.answer: No. It helps build, follow, and improve runbooks, but it should not replace organization-specific procedures.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Start with impact, symptoms, timestamps, recent changes, affected services, and sanitized evidence from logs, metrics, or traces.
